summary.tldr: Sets federal rules for post-secondary funding to provinces and requires a plan to split the Canada Social Transfer into social services and post-secondary parts.
what_it_does: Sets criteria that provincial post-secondary institutions must meet, including non-profit public administration, academic independence, quality, and accessibility, before a cash contribution may be made.
Lets Quebec choose not to follow the criteria in section 5 and still receive the cash contribution.
Requires provinces to give the minister prescribed information to qualify for funding.
Sets a default process where the minister can notify a province, seek more information, discuss the issue, and refer it to the Governor in Council, which may reduce or withhold funding.
Requires the minister to report to Parliament each year on the act, including funding amounts and indicators such as tuition, student debt, class sizes, faculty ratios, and financial aid.

Requires the minister, within six months, to work with provincial ministers to create a framework dividing the Canada Social Transfer into two parts, one for social assistance and social services and one for post-secondary education.
summary.background: The bill says cash contributions may be made to provinces under other Acts of Parliament. It also calls for a framework to divide the Canada Social Transfer into two distinct components.
